n: Book Five of the Psalms opens with a great thanksgiving hymn. The familiar refrain — God is good and his covenant love endures forever — sets the theme.
Those whom God has ‘redeemed’ — rescued and bought back — should say so out loud. Testimony is the natural response to deliverance.

f.w: Let the redeemed of the LORD say so

n: God gathered his people from every direction. This fits the return from exile and is echoed in latter-day revelation on the gathering of Israel.

f.w: gathered them out of the lands

n: The first of four pictures of rescue: travelers lost in the desert, unable to find a town to live in.
Hungry and thirsty, they were close to fainting. Their whole life was ebbing away.
This first refrain appears four times: in their trouble they cried to the Lord, and he rescued them.

f.w: they cried unto the LORD in their trouble

n: God led them on a straight road to a city where they could settle.
The second refrain, also repeated four times: if only people would thank the Lord for his steadfast love and wonders.

f.w: Oh that men would praise the LORD

n: God satisfies the thirsty and hungry with good things — both body and soul. Jesus promised the same to those who hunger for righteousness.

f.w: filleth the hungry soul with goodness

n: The second picture: prisoners sitting in darkness, chained in suffering and iron.
Their captivity came because they rebelled against God’s words and despised his counsel.
God humbled them with hard labor; they stumbled with no one to help. Sometimes hardship turns people back to God.
Yet when they cried out, he saved them.

f.w: he saved them out of their distresses

n: He led them out of the darkness and snapped their chains. Latter-day Saints also see in this Christ’s power to free the captive and the dead.
The praise refrain repeats: thank him for his goodness.
God smashes bronze gates and cuts through iron bars — nothing can hold his people when he frees them.
The third picture: people who became sick through their own foolish sin.

f.g: Those who act senselessly and sinfully.

n: They lost all appetite and came close to death’s gates.
The refrain again: they cried, and he saved them.
God ‘sent his word’ and healed them. Christians see the ultimate fulfillment in Jesus, the Word made flesh, who healed with a word.

f.w: He sent his word, and healed them

n: Thanks again for God’s goodness and wonders.
Those healed should offer thank-offerings and joyfully tell what God has done.
The fourth picture: sailors and merchants who travel the wide sea. Israel was not a seafaring nation, so the sea seemed especially dangerous.

f.w: go down to the sea in ships

n: Out on the deep, they witness God’s mighty works.
At God’s command a storm wind rises and lifts the waves high.
Ships rise to the sky and plunge to the depths; the sailors’ courage melts away.
They stagger like drunk men, and all their skill is useless — literally, ‘all their wisdom is swallowed up.’

f.g: Hebrew: ‘all their wisdom is swallowed up.’

n: Then they cry to the Lord, and he brings them out.

f.w: Then they cry unto the LORD

n: He hushes the storm to a whisper and the waves fall still — just as Jesus did on the Sea of Galilee.

f.w: He maketh the storm a calm

n: The sailors rejoice in the quiet, and God guides them to the harbor they longed for.
The final praise refrain for God’s goodness and wonders.

f.w: Oh that men would praise the LORD

n: Praise should be public — in the assembly of the people and among the leaders.
The psalm turns to a wisdom reflection: God can turn rivers into desert and springs into dry ground.

f.w: He turneth rivers into a wilderness

n: Fertile land can become a salty wasteland because of its people’s wickedness — as with Sodom and Gomorrah.
He can also do the reverse: turn desert into pools and dry ground into springs.

f.w: the wilderness into a standing water

n: There he settles the hungry, who build a city to live in.
They plant fields and vineyards that produce a rich harvest.
God blesses them with many children and flourishing herds.
But fortunes can reverse: people may be reduced and humbled by oppression and sorrow.
God pours contempt on proud rulers and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.
Meanwhile he lifts the needy out of their affliction and makes their families grow like flocks.

f.w: setteth he the poor on high

n: The upright will see this and be glad, while the wicked are left speechless.

f.w: all iniquity shall stop her mouth

n: The closing lesson: the wise will pay attention to these patterns and come to understand the Lord’s steadfast love.
